title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 258
paragraphs: About Heracles I heard the account that he was one of the twelve gods; but of the other Heracles whom the Hellenes know I was not able to hear anything in any part of Egypt. Moreover, to prove that the Egyptians did not take the name of Heracles from the Hellenes, but rather the Hellenes from the Egyptians — I mean those of the Hellenes who gave the name Heracles to the son of Amphitryon — of this, besides many other proofs, there is chiefly this: that the parents of this Heracles, Amphitryon and Alcmene, were both of Egyptian descent; and also that the Egyptians say they know neither the name of Poseidon nor of the Dioscuri, nor have these been accepted by them as gods among their other gods. Yet if they had received the name of any divinity from the Hellenes, they would naturally have preserved the memory of these most of all — assuming, as I suppose and as my judgment compels me to think, that in those times, as now, some of the Hellenes made voyages and were seafaring folk; so that the Egyptians would have learnt the names of these gods even more than that of Heracles. In fact, however, Heracles is a very ancient Egyptian god; and (as the Egyptians themselves say) it is seventeen thousand years to the beginning of the reign of Amasis from the time when the twelve gods — of whom they count Heracles one — were begotten of the eight gods.
